title: Choose with if
summary: Haskell: Choose with if. Try message 3. Try a small example and check what happens.
introduction: An if expression always has then and else parts because it must produce a value.

blocks.text: Install GHC. Save one example as lesson.hs and run runghc lesson.hs. Keep any definitions above main in the same file.

blocks.title: Choose with if
blocks.code:
message score = if score >= 5 then "Pass" else "Try again"
main = putStrLn (message 8)

blocks.text: The true condition returns Pass for putStrLn to write.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Both branches must produce the same kind of value.
